Riddhi Steel & Tube Ltd trades at a price-to-book multiple of 3.32x, which sits at a substantial premium compared to the sector benchmark of 2.37x [E7]. This elevated price-to-book valuation is difficult to justify given that the company's return on equity of 15.57% actually lags behind the sector benchmark of 17.52% [E9]. Furthermore, historical performance reveals a concerning long-term trend of mediocre profitability, highlighted by a median return on equity of just 9% over a 10-year period [E25] and a low return on equity of 13.1% over the last 3 years [E62]. Income-focused investors receive no immediate cash return from the business, as evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company's P/E of 21.3x trades at a discount to the sector benchmark of 25.04x [E1, E6], and its ROA of 0% slightly outperforms the sector benchmark of -0.8% [E8].

The bear's focus on the price-to-book multiple overlooks the more meaningful earnings valuation, where the company trades at a P/E of 21.3x against a sector benchmark of 25.04x [E1, E6]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio of 3.32x sits above the sector benchmark of 2.37x [E7]. However, the bear's dismissal of profitability based on long-term historical medians ignores the clear acceleration in recent performance: the median return on equity has stepped up from a 10-year median of 9% [E25] and a 3-year figure of 13.1% [E62, E27] to an annual ROE of 16.9% [E13] and a recent median of 17% [E28], closing in on the sector benchmark of 17.52% [E9]. Furthermore, the lack of a dividend [E4] is entirely consistent with a high-growth compounding phase that is actively generating this expanding equity return. Finally, the company demonstrates superior asset efficiency compared to its peers, delivering an ROA of 0% that beats the negative sector benchmark of -0.8% [E8].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 21.3x which is modestly below the sector benchmark of 25.04x [E1, E6]. However, the bull's reliance on this multiple ignores the premium price-to-book ratio of 3.32x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.37x [E7], alongside an asset-level return of 0% [E8] which hardly justifies paying 3.31x book value [E2] for a ₹ 244 Cr enterprise [E3]. While the bull points to an improving recent ROE of 16.9% [E13] and 17% [E28], these must be weighed against a 10-year median ROE of just 9% [E25] and an official flag noting a low 3-year return on equity of 13.1% [E62], exposing the recent bump as cyclical rather than structural compounding. Furthermore, dismissing the 0.00% dividend yield [E4] as a sign of a high-growth compounding phase is speculative, as the evidence shows no capital return to shareholders while trading near the upper middle of its range at 65% of its 52-week high-low span [E5]. Finally, the ROE of 15.57% still lags the sector benchmark of 17.52% [E9], demonstrating that the business remains inferior to peers despite the bull's selective reading of recent data points.
